cards.b: A set of observations of a variable taken at regular intervals of time.
The general direction of the data over time (increasing, decreasing or steady).
A pattern that repeats every cycle, e.g. high sales every summer.
Smooths out seasonal variation to show the trend.

cards.f: Number of points in a moving average
cards.b: Same as the length of the cycle: 4 for quarterly, 3 for termly, 12 for monthly data.

cards.f: How many moving averages from n values?
Where to plot a 3-point moving average
cards.b: At the middle of the three time periods it covers.

cards.f: Where to plot a 4-point moving average
cards.b: Halfway between the 2nd and 3rd of the four values.
A straight line of best fit by eye through the plotted moving averages, not through the original data.
The average increase (or decrease) per time period.
Actual value − trend value (moving average). Can be negative.
The mean of all seasonal variations for one season, e.g. all Quarter 1 values.
Trend value at the future time + mean seasonal variation for that season.
Less reliable the further into the future (extrapolation) or if the pattern changes.
Say it in context, e.g. 'sales are generally increasing over the three years'. Do not describe the seasonal ups and downs.

short.q: Termly sales are 30, 42, 36, 33, 45, 39. Calculate the 3-point moving averages. [3]
Quarterly values are 20, 30, 26, 24, 28, 38. Calculate the 4-point moving averages and state where the first is plotted. [3]
short.model: 25, 27, 29. The first is plotted halfway between the 2nd and 3rd values (between Q2 and Q3).

short.q: The actual values for Quarter 2 in three years are 58, 62 and 66, with trend values 50, 54 and 59. Calculate the mean seasonal variation for Quarter 2 (to 2 d.p.). [3]
The trend line gives 120 for Quarter 4 of next year. The mean seasonal variation for Quarter 4 is −15.5. Predict the value. [2]
points: add mean seasonal variation to trend

short.q: Why is a 3-point moving average used for data recorded each term? Also say why a prediction far into the future is unreliable. [2]
short.model: Each year has 3 terms (the cycle length is 3), so a 3-point average removes the seasonal variation. Far-future predictions are extrapolation, and the pattern may change.
